::: {.intro}
# Associate Professor, Department of Economics, [University of Toronto](https://www.economics.utoronto.ca/){target="_blank"}

::: {.lead}
I am a macroeconomist working on how governments should tax and spend when
households and firms differ sharply from one another. My research builds
quantitative models with incomplete markets and rich heterogeneity, and uses
them to characterise optimal policy — how income taxes and public debt should
be set when households face risk they cannot insure against, how climate policy
should be designed when its burden falls unevenly, and how countries should tax
multinational firms that shift profits across borders. A second strand studies
firms directly: the shift of US business activity toward pass-through forms,
and how uncertainty and borrowing constraints shape firm dynamics.
:::
